All right. Why not? Let's do this.

So, a few years ago I built a web site for writers. Part of this site included a forum. As might be expected, writers wrote a lot on that forum. Eventually, some cliques formed. Not a big deal that friendships would come of things, so I tried to keep things open and welcoming for newcomers. For a couple of years, things went well.

Unfortunately, at some point a writer -- who was very well-educated and a little snooty toward his "lessers" -- got a little too out of hand with his baiting. It was actually kind of impressive. His mastery of language meant that he could write a seemingly normal post that would have some erudite dig at a member of the forum, and 99% of people couldn't even catch on. But the target of his attack would catch it. And so this writer got into repeated trouble. I warned him a bit, but never kicked him off.

Then, he baited the wrong guy. This dude was a blue-collar hot-head who could not keep up with the big words that my genius troublemaker threw at him. So they fought. One (our genius) would write very apologetic (sounding) replies, but always with a passive-aggressive style, or with a backhanded compliment that most of us would miss. The other would write, "I'll find you and punch you in the face." Well, that was of course not okay to threaten people like that even if it was just a fake threat because he was pissy. So, I removed the offending posts and reminded people "no threats of violence." And then shit went bad.

First, the writers screamed bloody murder about censorship and burning of books and Fahrenheit 451 and blah blah blah. It was a frenzy, total chaos on the forums. When I tried to explain that I was trying to keep them from physical harm, that just infuriated them more. Imagine waves of posts about nanny states and autonomy and parenting and condescension and so on. I was accused of every bad thing.

So next, Mr. Punchy seized upon that moment to coordinate every member leaving en masse. This didn't work well, because he had a reputation for being Mr. Punchy. But it worked a little, because everyone was livid that I had tried to protect the forum from threats of violence. Unfortunately, maybe similar to Voat (ouch! sorry!), the flight of members from my site to the competitor sorta petered out a little. I mean, the other site got a wave of angry members, but it wasn't sustained growth, so it looked more like a bunch of angry complainers just took over an unrelated forum to bitch & moan about my site, and they weren't otherwise plugged into that community. They sorta overran it, and eventually wore out their welcome.

Meanwhile my site kept going, and grew. And Mr. Punchy got even angrier about that. So he doxxed me. He had been banned by that point, so he made a new account and posted piles of my private info during a 3 day weekend when he knew I was out of town. I removed it and banned him again. At this point, some of his troublemaking friends who had left with him (and who were eventually banned for doxxing/threats/etcetera) starting sending me messages saying they regretted their move and wanted back in. I agreed, if they could talk some sense into the guy, because he was now constantly trying to "hack" my site (hack in quotes because don't forget he was blue collar for a reason -- the complexity of something like programming was simply out of his league) and making threats. This backfired.

Mr. Punchy was fucking hostile over his "friends" trying to talk sense into him. He blamed me, and did two things. 1) He threatened to sue me. I laughed that off. That made him madder. So, he tried for #2: He sent me my home address in an email, with the words, "If I cannot get satisfaction within the law, I will go outside of the law. I know where your wife & kids live."

At that point, things ended rapidly. I'd had enough. I did 3 things:

  • I gave up the web site entirely. I just went from being self-employed and running that site to being an employee of someone else. The site still exists, but it's just anarchy with no moderation and eventually people left. I couldn't deal with that level of bullshit. File it under "This is why we can't have nice things."
  • I called the cops and got a restraining order. This apparently freaked out Mr. Punchy. I don't understand how restraining orders even work, but somehow when I filed mine, it got back to his wife or someone? I don't know, but suddenly people in the real world knew he was being a dick and he got super ashamed. But I didn't stop there.
  • I sued. This wasn't a real lawsuit, not what you traditionally think of anyway. It's a pre-emptive suit. I can't recall the name of it now, maybe a reader can help me, but this is the lawsuit type where you go to the judge and say, "Someone is planning on suing me, or threatening it, and I think they're full of shit. I think a judge would file in my favor. So, let's force the issue, right now. Drag that dude who is making threats into court and issue a pre-emptive judgement." The reason this is useful? It forces a person in another state to fly out to defend his hot-headed words that he didn't think he'd actually have to back up. So, I lost a bunch of cash lawyering up. But I went in knowing that. He got surprised. He blew tons of cash that he didn't expect to spend, and in the end, he failed and I got my favorable judgement.

Although in the end I "won" and got a peaceful ending, I regret pretty much all of it. It was actually probably a full year of my life given over to a miserable conflict with a miserable person and I lost money, happiness, and was honestly scared for my life and the lives of my family. It ruined my love for my own business and pet projects, and they've now languished in an uncared state for years. So if I had to do it all over again, I would laugh the moment people got that fucking worked up over a forum argument, and I would have washed my hands of the whole matter and bailed right the fuck out.

It's also worth remembering the difference between your disagreement with the law, the government, and with the police.
